question: By what percentage was Paul di Resta's fastest-lap speed in race 853 higher than in race 854? Use the speed in race 854 as the baseline and round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId = 853 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS DECIMAL(12,4)) END) - MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId = 854 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS DECIMAL(12,4)) END)) / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId = 854 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS DECIMAL(12,4)) END), 0), 2) FROM drivers AS d JOIN results AS r ON r.driverId = d.driverId WHERE d.forename = 'Paul' AND d.surname = 'di Resta' AND r.raceId IN (853, 854)

question: I'm writing an article about the Italian Grand Prix and want to know which first names recur among the drivers who finished second in that race. For every forename carried by two or more runners-up of the Italian Grand Prix across all its editions in the data, please give me one row with the forename and the number of runners-up who carried it. Order the rows from the most runners-up to the fewest, and alphabetically by forename when two forenames are tied. Leave out any forename held by only one runner-up.
evidence: A runner-up is the driver who finished second in an edition of the Italian Grand Prix.
SQL: SELECT d.forename AS forename, COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) AS runner_ups FROM races AS r INNER JOIN results AS x ON x.raceId = r.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverId = x.driverId WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND x.position = 2 GROUP BY d.forename HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) > 1 ORDER BY runner_ups DESC, d.forename

question: I'm researching the generation of drivers born in the 1980s and want to know how much final-session qualifying that generation actually did as a whole cohort. How many Q3 lap times did a driver born between 1981 and 1991 set on average? Count every driver born in that period in the average, including any who never set a Q3 lap time. Please give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session of a race weekend, whose times decide the top starting grid positions.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(COUNT(q.q3 > '' OR NULL) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId), 2) AS avg_q3_times_per_driver FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN qualifying q ON q.driverId = d.driverId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', d.dob) BETWEEN '1981' AND '1991'

question: I'm profiling drivers whose first name alone doesn't identify them. Across all races in the dataset throughout Formula 1 history, how many qualifying 1 times slower than two minutes were set by drivers who share their first name with at least one other driver and who have no code? I want just that single count.
evidence: A driver's code is their three-letter abbreviation (e.g. 'HAM'); having no code means no such abbreviation is on record for them. The qualifying 1 time is the time a driver set in the first qualifying session of a race, one per race they took part in.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE d.code IS NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM drivers o WHERE o.forename = d.forename AND o.driverId <> d.driverId) AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND (CAST(substr(q.q1, 1, instr(q.q1, ':') - 1) AS REAL) > 2 OR (CAST(substr(q.q1, 1, instr(q.q1, ':') - 1) AS REAL) = 2 AND CAST(substr(q.q1, instr(q.q1, ':') + 1) AS REAL) > 0))

question: I'm checking how much of the championship points for drivers named Robert came from races covered by the lap-by-lap timing archive. For every driver whose forename is Robert, I need their reference name and the total points they scored in races where lap-by-lap timing data exists for that driver in that race. The totals should cover all seasons and races on record.
evidence: The reference name is the driver's short identifier, and points are championship points recorded for that driver's race result.
SQL: SELECT d.driverRef AS reference_name, COALESCE(SUM(r.points), 0) AS total_points FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN results r ON r.driverId = d.driverId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lapTimes l WHERE l.raceId = r.raceId AND l.driverId = d.driverId) WHERE d.forename = 'Robert' GROUP BY d.driverId, d.driverRef ORDER BY total_points DESC, reference_name

question: Who set the fastest time in Q3 (the final qualifying session) at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? Please give me the driver's reference name (the short identifier like 'hamilton') as the result. If two drivers set the same fastest Q3 time, give me both of their reference names.
evidence: Q3: the final qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend
SQL: SELECT d.driverRef FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3 != '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE raceId = q.raceId AND q3 IS NOT NULL AND q3 != '')

question: I'm studying how pit stop activity changed across the refuelling-rule change for Australia's F1 drivers. For each season from 2002 through 2013, can you give me the total number of pit stops made at the races of that season where, after the race, at least one Australian driver was placed better than 20th in the driver standings? I'd like the season year and the total pit stop count for each season. The pit stop total should cover every driver who pitted at those races, not just the Australian drivers.
evidence: Better than 20th in the driver standings means a position of 1 through 19 after that race. A pit stop is any recorded pit stop made by any driver at the race.
SQL: WITH oz_races AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.raceId, r.year FROM races AS r INNER JOIN driverStandings AS ds ON ds.raceId = r.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverId = ds.driverId WHERE d.nationality = 'Australian' AND ds.position <= 19 AND r.year BETWEEN 2002 AND 2013) SELECT oz.year AS season, COUNT(ps.stop) AS pit_stops FROM oz_races AS oz LEFT JOIN pitStops AS ps ON ps.raceId = oz.raceId GROUP BY oz.year ORDER BY oz.year

question: I'm looking into fastest race laps recorded by drivers born in the 1980s. Can you tell me which three drivers born between 1980 and 1990 reached the highest single fastest-lap speed at any point in their career? I'd like their first and last names, ranked from the highest career-high speed down, and if two drivers are tied on that speed, list the one born earlier first, and then the one whose last name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the three names, nothing else.
evidence: Fastest lap speed: the average speed, in km/h, that a driver recorded on their single fastest lap of a race. A driver's career-high speed is based on that one lap, not an average across their laps.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM drivers AS d JOIN results AS r ON r.driverId = d.driverId WHERE SUBSTR(d.dob, 1, 4) BETWEEN '1980' AND '1990' AND r.fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname, d.dob ORDER BY MAX(CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL)) DESC, d.dob, d.surname LIMIT 3

question: What is the ratio of the Advertisement budget for the Yearly Kickoff meeting to that for the October Meeting?
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff' THEN T1.amount ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T2.event_name = 'October Meeting' THEN T1.amount ELSE 0 END) FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN event AS T2 ON T1.link_to_event = T2.event_id WHERE T1.category = 'Advertisement' AND T2.type = 'Meeting'

question: I'm putting together a review of last fall's activities and want to see how the Women's Soccer game compared to a typical event that semester. Please give me one row with: the number of students who attended the Women's Soccer event, the average number of students who attended events held in fall 2019 rounded to one decimal place, and a verdict of 'more', 'fewer' or 'equal' comparing the Women's Soccer head count to that average. Fall 2019 means events from 1 September 2019 through 30 November 2019 inclusive, and every event that semester counts toward the average even if nobody attended it. The verdict should compare the Women's Soccer head count to the rounded average: above it is 'more', below is 'fewer', exactly equal is 'equal'.
evidence: Women's Soccer is an event name; attendance at an event is the number of members who attended it.
SQL: WITH fall_events AS (SELECT e.event_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance AS a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS attendees FROM event AS e WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2019-12-01'), agg AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(attendees), 1) AS avg_att FROM fall_events), soccer AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS head_count FROM attendance AS a JOIN event AS e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e.event_name = 'Women''s Soccer') SELECT s.head_count AS soccer_attendance, g.avg_att AS average_attendance, CASE WHEN s.head_count > g.avg_att THEN 'more' WHEN s.head_count < g.avg_att THEN 'fewer' ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict FROM soccer AS s CROSS JOIN agg AS g;

question: Our officer team wants to settle a debate about whether we pull more weight than the rest of the club, so we need the attendance numbers before the next meeting. Could you tell us two things: the average number of events attended per officer, and the average number of events attended per other student, each rounded to two decimal places? To be clear on who counts where: officers are the members holding the position of President, Vice President, Secretary, or Treasurer, and everyone else in the club counts as an other student. Each average should cover every member of its group, and include every event in the club's records - there's no date cutoff.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(a.link_to_event) AS cnt FROM member m LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position) SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.position IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') THEN t.cnt END), 2) AS officer_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.position NOT IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') THEN t.cnt END), 2) AS other_students_avg FROM t

question: I'm reconciling what we budgeted for September events against what we actually spent. Can you give me the total amount budgeted for the September 2019 events that served pizza? By September 2019 I mean events dated September 1 through September 30, 2019. An event counts as having served pizza if pizza was among the expenses booked to it. Please include every budget line for those events, whatever the category - not just the food lines. All I need back is the single dollar figure for that total.
evidence: A pizza expense means an expense whose description is Pizza.
SQL: WITH pizza_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT b.link_to_event AS event_id FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE e.expense_description = 'Pizza'), sept_events AS (SELECT event_id FROM event WHERE event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND event_date < '2019-10-01') SELECT ROUND(SUM(b.amount), 2) AS total_budgeted FROM budget b JOIN sept_events s ON s.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT event_id FROM pizza_events)

question: Among our closed events that stayed within budget (total spending not exceeding total budget), which one had the most purchases? Please give me just that event's name. Consider every closed event that didn't go over budget, including events with no purchases at all. If two events tie for the most purchases, report only the one with the alphabetically first event ID.
evidence: A purchase is a single item recorded on an expense record; one expense record may list several items. Total budget is the sum of budgeted amounts across all budget lines of the event; total spending is the sum of spent amounts across all budget lines of the event.
SQL: WITH budget_totals AS (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(spent) AS total_spending, SUM(amount) AS total_budget FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event), items AS (SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(LENGTH(x.expense_description) - LENGTH(REPLACE(x.expense_description, ',', '')) + 1) AS purchases FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget GROUP BY b.link_to_event) SELECT e.event_name FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget_totals bt ON bt.link_to_event = e.event_id LEFT JOIN items i ON i.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.status = 'Closed' AND (bt.total_budget IS NULL OR bt.total_spending <= bt.total_budget) GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name ORDER BY COALESCE(i.purchases, 0) DESC, e.event_id LIMIT 1

question: For every event in the club's records, can you give me the event name, event date, total amount budgeted for the event, and the number of members who attended it? Please sort the list by event name, then by event date, both in ascending order.
SQL: SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, COALESCE(b.total_budgeted_amount, 0) AS total_budgeted_amount, COALESCE(a.attendee_count, 0) AS attendee_count FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) AS total_budgeted_amount FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC

question: I'm putting together the end-of-term spending review. Who bought the most different kinds of items in October or November 2019? Please give me that member's full name, how many different kinds of items they bought in those two months, and their total spending in dollars over the same period. If two members tie for the most kinds, list every tied member with their kind count and spending.
evidence: An item is one of the individual things a purchase covered, such as a pizza or a bottle of water.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split AS (SELECT link_to_member, expense_description AS rest FROM expense WHERE expense_date BETWEEN '2019-10-01' AND '2019-11-30' UNION ALL SELECT link_to_member, SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest || ',', ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> ''), items AS (SELECT link_to_member, TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest || ',', ',') - 1)) AS item FROM split WHERE rest <> ''), kinds AS (SELECT link_to_member, COUNT(DISTINCT item) AS kind_count FROM items GROUP BY link_to_member), spend AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(cost) AS total_spending FROM expense WHERE expense_date BETWEEN '2019-10-01' AND '2019-11-30' GROUP BY link_to_member) SELECT m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name, k.kind_count, s.total_spending FROM kinds k JOIN spend s ON s.link_to_member = k.link_to_member JOIN member m ON m.member_id = k.link_to_member WHERE k.kind_count = (SELECT MAX(kind_count) FROM kinds)

question: I'm building a fact box on Marvel heroes' civilian identities. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose full name (their civilian identity, like 'Richard Milhouse Jones') is known, which superpower is the most common, and how many of those heroes have it? If several superpowers tie for most common, list all of them with their counts. Just give me the superpower name(s) and the counts.
SQL: WITH pc AS (SELECT sp.power_name, COUNT(DISTINCT hp.hero_id) AS hero_count FROM hero_power hp JOIN superpower sp ON hp.power_id = sp.id JOIN superhero s ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' GROUP BY sp.power_name) SELECT power_name, hero_count FROM pc WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM pc) ORDER BY power_name

question: I'm putting together a comparison of the heaviest brick-strength characters. What is the average weight, in kilograms, of all superheroes whose Strength score equals the Hulk's? I just need a single integer rounded to the nearest kilogram. Include every superhero in the database, no restrictions on publisher or alignment. If a hero's weight is unknown, leave them out and average only over the heroes whose weight has actually been measured.
evidence: Strength is one of the six measured hero attributes, each scored on a 1-100 scale; the Hulk is the superhero named 'Hulk'; weight is the superhero's weight in kilograms.
SQL: SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS INTEGER) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s INNER JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id INNER JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT ha2.attribute_value FROM superhero s2 INNER JOIN hero_attribute ha2 ON ha2.hero_id = s2.id INNER JOIN attribute a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE s2.superhero_name = 'Hulk' AND a2.attribute_name = 'Strength') AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: What is the average weight in kilograms of the DC Comics heroes whose eye colour is also shared by at least one Marvel Comics hero? Leave out any heroes whose weight is unknown, round the result to the nearest kilogram, and treat 'No Colour' as an eye colour like any other when matching between publishers. I just want that single number.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND s.eye_colour_id IN (SELECT s2.eye_colour_id FROM superhero AS s2 JOIN publisher AS p2 ON s2.publisher_id = p2.id WHERE p2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics')

question: Which race is the most common among the superheroes published by the same publisher as the superhero whose full name is Charles Chandler? I'd like, for that publisher's superheroes only, the name of the most common race and the count of that publisher's superheroes of that race. Ignore any superhero with no race recorded. If several races tie for most common, list every tied race with its count.
evidence: Race: the superhero's species or type, e.g. Human, Mutant, Alien.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT r.race AS race, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE full_name = 'Charles Chandler') AND r.race <> '-' GROUP BY r.id, r.race) SELECT race, hero_count FROM counts WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM counts)

question: I'm writing a power-profile feature on heroes with super speed or death touch. Can you give me one number: the average intelligence score of the superheroes who have either of those powers? Round it to one decimal place, and only count the heroes who actually have an intelligence score in the database.
evidence: "Super speed" and "death touch" are superpower names as used in the database; "intelligence" is the hero attribute by that name.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(v), 1) AS average_intelligence FROM (SELECT DISTINCT T1.id, T4.attribute_value AS v FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_power AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN superpower AS T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T4 ON T4.hero_id = T1.id INNER JOIN attribute AS T5 ON T4.attribute_id = T5.id WHERE T3.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch') AND T5.attribute_name = 'Intelligence')

question: I'm profiling publisher rosters and now want to look at the physical build of George Lucas's heroes. What is the average height of the heroes he created, in centimetres, and their average weight, in kilograms? Please round each average to one decimal place, and only include heroes whose height (for the height average) or weight (for the weight average) is actually known.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END), 1) AS average_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 1) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas'

question: I'm auditing identity info on our hero profile pages. How many neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name? Just give me the count.
evidence: By "full name" I mean the hero's real-world identity name, not the superhero/costume name.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neutral_heroes_with_known_full_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Neutral' AND T1.full_name IS NOT NULL AND T1.full_name <> '-'

question: Among patients followed at the outpatient clinic who ever had an abnormal anti-SSA result, which one showed the highest anti-RNP titer? Please give me the patient's ID and the anti-RNP titer value. This should cover the hospital's full records across all years, and if several patients tie for the highest anti-RNP titer, list every one of them.
evidence: Abnormal anti-SSA means any SSA result other than negative or 0. "Followed at the outpatient clinic" is the admission status marked with a minus sign. Anti-RNP titer is the strength of the anti-ribonuclear protein result.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Admission = '-' AND T2.SSA IS NOT NULL AND T2.SSA NOT IN ('negative', '0')), titers AS (SELECT T.ID, T.RNP FROM Laboratory AS T JOIN cohort AS C ON T.ID = C.ID WHERE T.RNP IS NOT NULL AND T.RNP <> 'negative') SELECT DISTINCT ID, RNP FROM titers WHERE CAST(RNP AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) FROM titers)

question: I'm putting together a demographic summary of our low-albumin patients. Could you tell me how many patients with an albumin measurement below 3.5 are female and how many are male? I'd like one row per sex group showing the sex (F or M) and the number of patients in that group.
evidence: F stands for female and M stands for male.
SQL: SELECT T1.SEX AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALB < 3.5 AND T1.SEX IN ('F','M') GROUP BY T1.SEX ORDER BY T1.SEX

question: How many patients in our thrombosis ward are followed at the outpatient clinic (rather than admitted) with a normal Rheumatoid Factor and no positive measure of degree of coagulation? Please give me a single number. For context: a normal Rheumatoid Factor is '-' or '+-', a positive measure of degree of coagulation is '+' on any of the coagulation measures (KCT, RVVT, LAC), and an outpatient-clinic patient is one with Admission = '-'. If a patient has no recorded coagulation measure, count them as having no positive measure.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS T1 WHERE T1.Admission = '-' AND T1.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IN ('-', '+-')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination E WHERE E.ID = T1.ID AND (E.KCT = '+' OR E.RVVT = '+' OR E.LAC = '+'))

question: I'm putting together a cohort summary and need one number: how many patients followed at the outpatient clinic (admission marker '-') have a most recent IgG lab result of 2000 or higher? By most recent, I mean the IgG measurement with the greatest laboratory date for that patient - since a patient has at most one lab record per date, there should be no ambiguity.
SQL: WITH latest_igg AS (SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS LastDate FROM Laboratory WHERE IGG IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID) SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p JOIN latest_igg AS li ON li.ID = p.ID JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = li.ID AND l.Date = li.LastDate WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.IGG >= 2000

question: I'm putting together a renal-involvement review. Could you pull the demographics of patients who show both marked tissue damage and clinically significant proteinuria? Specifically, I need the patient ID, sex, and birthday of every patient who has at least one LDH result of 500 or higher and at least one urinary protein result of 100 mg/dL or more. A few details: an LDH of exactly 500 counts, and a urinary protein of exactly 100 mg/dL counts. The qualifying LDH and the qualifying urinary protein don't have to come from the same lab visit. Please give me one row per patient, ordered by patient ID, and nothing beyond those three fields.
evidence: Urinary protein is reported in mg/dL; a dipstick grade may carry the equivalent concentration in mg/dL in parentheses, e.g. '+2(100)' is 100 mg/dL. A result written as '>=' followed by a value means at least that many mg/dL, e.g. '>=300' is 300 mg/dL or more. 'TR' means a trace and '-' means none detected; any other marker is not a quantified mg/dL concentration. An LDH of 500 or higher is outside the normal range.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT p.ID, p.SEX, p.Birthday FROM Patient AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.LDH >= 500) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS u WHERE u.ID = p.ID AND CASE WHEN u.`U-PRO` LIKE '%(%' THEN CAST(substr(u.`U-PRO`, instr(u.`U-PRO`, '(')+1, instr(u.`U-PRO`, ')')-instr(u.`U-PRO`, '(')-1) AS REAL) WHEN u.`U-PRO` LIKE '>=%' THEN CAST(substr(u.`U-PRO`,3) AS REAL) ELSE CAST(u.`U-PRO` AS REAL) END >= 100) ORDER BY p.ID

question: How many female patients have a Sjögren's syndrome diagnosis recorded in a medical examination? Please count across the full examination history with no date restriction, and note that suspected cases don't count—only an actual SjS diagnosis should be included. I just need that single number.
evidence: SjS is the standard medical abbreviation for Sjögren's syndrome, and the diagnosis is recorded under that abbreviation.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) AS n_female_sjs_patients FROM Patient AS T1 JOIN Examination AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.SEX = 'F' AND (',' || REPLACE(T2.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') LIKE ('%' || ',' || 'SjS' || ',' || '%');

question: How many patients who were never admitted to the hospital (outpatient follow-up only) had at least one normal anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) result? A normal RNP result means the test found no anti-ribonuclear protein antibody: a negative result, or a measured value of zero. I just need a single number.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody test
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.RNP IN ('negative', '0')

question: I'd like to know, among patients who have at least one normal anti-SM laboratory result (recorded as 'negative' or '0') and whose examinations show no thrombosis, how many have ever had significant proteinuria on any laboratory record. Significant proteinuria means 30 mg/dl or more; '-' and 'TR' count as no proteinuria. I only need the number of such patients.
evidence: anti-SM: normal is recorded as 'negative' or '0'; proteinuria is measured semi-quantitatively as '-', 'TR', or the approximate daily urinary protein excretion in mg/dl
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.SM IN ('negative', '0')) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination AS e WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e.Thrombosis = 0) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination AS e WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e.Thrombosis <> 0) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND CAST(l."U-PRO" AS REAL) >= 30)
